transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Lina Park (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (LucentOps Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (LucentOps Platform), Jordan Blake (LucentOps FinOps), Priya Singh (LucentOps Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): quick demo of console route lenses, drilling into cost per route and per model, showing Optimize suggestions; customers asked about SSO, KMS, and hybrid deployment.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll demo the Console lenses for per-route usage and cost attribution, really quick intro then Ethan will show the live UI.
[00:16] Maya: Sounds good, trying to squeeze this in between standups, so appreciate it.
[00:22] Ethan: Cool, so first slide, top-level — usage by route, you can see traffic, p95 latency, and token spend side-by-side. We call these "lenses" because you can pivot by model, route, or customer id.
[00:39] Tom: Quick Q — will that show if a route is hitting dedicated or hosted capacity?
[00:44] Ethan: Yes, we surface deployment type per request, and you can filter to only dedicated capacity or cross-compare. There is an auto-fallback column so you can see when hosted was used as fallback.
[01:02] Jordan: Nice. How accurate is per-token cost? We need it to reconcile with our billing reports.
[01:08] Lina: We compute unit economics at token level using model profile + runtime telemetry; there is a small variance for batching effects but we have an attribution model that backfills. Typical variance is 2-5% depending on batching.
[01:23] Priya: Security question: where are logs retained? We have strict retention for PII, and KMS requirements.
[01:29] Sofia: Good callout. We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, SOC 2 compliance for hosted, and you can opt-out of storing request bodies. We'll share the SOC docs.
[01:44] Maya: For pilot we likely need VPC peering and to ensure audit logs ship to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[01:50] Ethan: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM, or in Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem. For hosted we'll provide streaming export to your logging endpoint.
[02:05] Ethan: Ok demo time — I'm in the Console, top nav -> Usage -> Route Lenses. Here you can see route /chat/compose is top consumer.
[02:20] [screen share noise, brief pause]
[02:28] Ethan: Zooming into that route, we show token volume, cost by model variant, p50/p95 latency, and error rate. The right column has "cost drivers" and shows prompt vs completion token split.
[02:47] Maya: Do you break out prompt vs completion? That split is key for our billing models.
[02:51] Ethan: Yep, split is shown and you can export CSV. Note: sometimes the transcriber shows "prompt" as "promt" in older exports, but here in UI it's explicit.
[03:05] Tom: For our mixed flows we have short prompts with long completions, do you recommend batching?
[03:10] Ethan: Batching helps throughput but can increase tail latency. Our Optimize tab gives suggestions: continuous batching for high qps routes, smaller batch windows for latency-sensitive ones, and quantization suggestions for cheaper model variants.
[03:26] Lina: Also worth calling out prefix/KV cache — for chat-heavy routes with repeated context we can serve from cache to reduce compute. Some of the K V cache notes might be munged in transcript as K V cash.
[03:40] Jordan: Interesting. We need to attribute spend to product lines; can we tag routes by team?
[03:44] Ethan: Yes tags are first-class. You can assign labels and then the console will roll up cost by tag. Works well with our per-token cost breakdown.
[04:00] Maya: Can we set alerts on route spend spikes?
[04:03] Sofia: Absolutely — alerts on cost or token rate thresholds, and we can set automatic fallback to cheaper model variants if cost exceeds thresholds.
[04:15] Tom: Fallback sounds risky for quality. Is there a canary policy?
[04:19] Lina: We support canary and A/B rollouts per route; fallback is policy-driven with tolerance windows and health checks.
[04:29] [05:00-ish] Ethan: Now jumping into the Cost Attribution view — this is where you can see cost per route and per model, and also an "attribution waterfall" that shows how batching, caching, and preemptible GPUs affected unit cost.
[05:48] Jordan: Waterfall sounds useful. Do you expose quantization level per model so we can reconcile accuracy vs cost?
[05:55] Ethan: Yes we surface model variant, quantization bits (e.g., int8,int4), and run historical perf so you can map quality regressions.
[06:10] Priya: On encryption for Dedicated — we need HSM-backed keys. Is that supported?
[06:15] Sofia: For Dedicated and Private we support HSM and customer-managed KMS. We'll attach the KMS integration notes in the follow-up.
[06:28] Maya: What about region-specific residency? Some of our EU traffic must stay in EU.
[06:33] Ethan: You can route by region and pin routes to region-specific capacity. We also respect model residency, you can pin a model version in a region.
[06:44] [07:00] Ethan: Switching to Optimize recommendations — the Console runs heuristics and model profiles to suggest batching/window sizes, caching policies, and whether to move to a quantized variant for a given route.
[07:18] Tom: Does Optimize simulate expected latency/cost before applying?
[07:22] Lina: It gives estimated delta based on historical traffic and model benchmarks. We recommend testing in a canary lane.
[07:33] Maya: For our workload we have many small multistep calls, will batching across conversation turns break semantics?
[07:40] Ethan: We respect call boundaries; continuous batching is across independent requests. For multi-turn you'll want to preserve kv cache semantics, which we do.
[07:52] [08:10] Jordan: You mentioned exporting CSV, can we pipe to BigQuery or Snowflake?
[08:15] Sofia: Yes we have connectors for BigQuery, Snowflake, and S3 exports for raw telemetry.
[08:24] Priya: Related to compliance, do you store raw prompts in hosted mode?
[08:28] Ethan: By default we retain minimal telemetry and redacted request bodies, but customers can disable storing request bodies. For full control use Private or Dedicated.
[08:40] Maya: Pilot scope — we want to test five routes: /compose, /summarize, /classify, /search, /recommend. We'll run one week of traffic.
[08:48] Sofia: Great — for pilot we'll enable per-route telemetry, Optimize suggestions, and send daily cost rollups.
[09:00] Ethan: I'll set up a dashboard template for those five routes and pre-populate tags for your teams.
[09:08] [09:30] Tom: On the pricing side, do you charge per-token for hosted and commit for dedicated?
[09:36] Sofia: Hosted is usage-based per token, embeddings per unit, and Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit. We can do hybrid where critical routes use Dedicated and others hit Hosted or burst.
[09:52] Jordan: How are bursts handled if Dedicated is saturated?
[09:56] Lina: Smart routing can spill to hosted or another region; you can set priority tiers so critical traffic stays on Dedicated. Spillover is metered and visible in the cost dashboard.
[10:10] [10:30] Ethan: Small demo of anomaly detection — console flagged a sudden spike on /search, we can view downstream examples, see exact token distribution and correlated cost.
[10:45] Maya: Can that auto-create a ticket or notify Slack?
[10:48] Sofia: Yes, alert actions include Slack, PagerDuty, or creating tickets in Jira.
[10:55] Priya: For audit purposes we need immutable logs for access to keys and admin actions.
[10:59] Ethan: Audit trail is exportable and immutable for Private/Dedicated, hosted retains audit logs for configurable windows depending on plan.
[11:12] [11:30] Jordan: For the token-level benchmark, will you run it against our anonymized traces?
[11:35] Ethan: We can accept anonymized traces or a synthetic workload. We'll run the benchmark in our testbed and provide per-token cost and latency numbers.
[11:46] Maya: What's the typical turnaround?
[11:49] Sofia: ~3 business days once we have traces and routing mapping.
[11:55] Tom: Any gotchas about telemetry overhead? Adding per-request tracing might add latency.
[11:59] Lina: We sample by default and can increase sampling for pilot; end-to-end impact is usually <1% but depends on payload size.
[12:12] [12:30] Ethan: Quick pointer — Console has an "Economics" export which shows hourly unit cost and shows adjustments from caching/batching. That helps you feed FinOps systems.
[12:40] Jordan: That's the kind of visibility we need.
[12:44] Maya: Ok, decision factors for us: security gating (KMS/HSM), pilot results for cost delta, and SLA targets for p95.
[12:52] Sofia: We'll align pilot to those success criteria.
[13:00] [13:30] Sofia: Let's recap next steps — we'll send pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, pilot runbook, and schedule kickoff next week.
[13:42] Ethan: I'll prep the dashboard template and runbook.
[13:48] Maya: We'll gather sample routes and traffic by Friday.
[14:00] [14:30] Priya: One more — can we get a summary of the fallback policy logic? We need to review for security and exposure.
[14:37] Lina: Yes I'll include policy docs in the follow-up.
[14:44] Jordan: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[14:50] Sofia: Thanks LucentOps team, we'll follow up with the packet.
[14:55] [call ended]

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash"), some speaker labels merged by the recorder.
